$comment: mergeDelivery.enqueueFailureSmellAfter (integer 1–100, standard 3) surfaces consecutive enqueue failures as a health smell; mergeDelivery.enqueueRetrySeconds (integer 1–3600, standard 60) sets exponential backoff capped at one hour. Both resolve standard < platform < tool independently; the drain logs their source. Refused/unconfirmed enqueues retain the verbatim GitHub message in the run record and never stamp clearance; conflict refusals enter the existing conflict finding/fixer path. mergeQueue.refreshOnUnsatisfiedWorkflows (on|off): when GitHub's merge queue refuses a green PR because required workflows are not satisfied (runs older than the ruleset), the drain refreshes the PR onto main once per head so fresh runs count, then enqueues it. off leaves the PR failing to enqueue. Env override: WE_MERGE_QUEUE_REFRESH_ON_UNSATISFIED_WORKFLOWS. mergeQueue.refreshOnStaleMergeGate (on|off, standard on): refresh a ready PR once per head when its only red required check is a head-bound merge-gate HOLD whose holds are now satisfied; enqueue only on a later green pass. Env override: WE_MERGE_QUEUE_REFRESH_ON_STALE_MERGE_GATE. mergeQueue.enqueueOnEvent {enabled, debounceSeconds, debounceMaxWaitMs} (card 257, standard {false, 15, 60000}): when the drain daemon's PR-events feed marks a PR of this repo with a green check suite or an added review:accepted / ready-to-merge label, the daemon runs the drain's single-PR fast drain (merge-ai-prs --only) for it debounceSeconds after the last such event or debounceMaxWaitMs after the first event of the burst, whichever comes first, between passes, instead of waiting for the next full pass. Every drain gate must pass. With drain.prestageWhileCiRuns (standard true), pending approved heads carrying ready-to-merge precompute the non-CI gates; green events can reuse that preparation for drain.prestageTtlMin (standard 30 minutes) before listing, after revalidating head, labels, body/base, required checks, the optional CodeQL gate and live red-team evidence. Stale preparation falls back to the full fast drain. Resolved via the policy cascade; env override WE_ENQUEUE_ON_EVENT=on|off. See we:scripts/lib/enqueue-on-event.mjs. mergeQueue.enqueueOnEvent.debounceMaxWaitMs (integer 1000–600000, standard 60000) caps debounce from the first eligible event; newer events preserve that start time. mergeQueue.enqueueOnEvent.timeoutSeconds (integer 60–3600, standard 600) stops a fast drain with SIGTERM after this duration and records a timeout outcome. mergeQueue.enqueueOnEvent.catchUp {enabled, intervalMinutes, concurrency, busyIntervalSeconds, maxQueued, missSmellAfter, order} (standard {false, 10, 3, 60, 12, 3, priority-then-first-accept}): on daemon start and then every intervalMinutes, list open ready-to-merge PRs of this repo that are not in GitHub's merge queue, priority class, then build.priority list order, then first acceptance on any head (ready time fallback), and run the same single-PR fast drain for each, never more than the merge queue has room for (catchUp.maxQueued minus the PRs already queued; mergeDelivery.batchSize still controls parallel builds). Run up to catchUp.concurrency single-PR drains concurrently (1 preserves serial operation), rechecking live room before each start; the drain owns serialized numbering/branch writes and live batching admission. A batching deferral stops new starts without cancelling active siblings. After a round completes, retry after busyIntervalSeconds while room and runnable, unqueued, non-backed-off PRs remain; use intervalMinutes when nothing is runnable. After every fast drain that reports enqueued the daemon re-reads GitHub's isInMergeQueue; a PR that did not enter counts a miss and is retried next catch-up; missSmellAfter consecutive misses (standard 3) log a SMELL enqueue-not-entering line. mergeQueue.enqueueOnEvent.catchUp.timeoutBackoffRounds (nonnegative integer, standard 3; 0 disables) skips the next N catch-up listings after a fast-drain timeout unless its head or checks change; events bypass the hold. mergeQueue.enqueueOnEvent.catchUp.missBackoff {enabled, ttlMinutes} (standard {true, 30}, ttlMinutes integer 1–1440): skip repeated hold-eligible catch-up misses (explicit enqueue outcome kinds red-team-pending, sent-back, or bornas-collision) until the head or sorted labels change or TTL expires; queue contention, independent retry timers, unreadable evidence, unclassified revalidation aborts and unknown kinds retry next catch-up. Events bypass, enabled:false restores every-round retries. Resolves nested leaves independently via the policy cascade and logs their sources. mergeQueue.fastDrain.scope (target|full, standard target, env WE_FAST_DRAIN_SCOPE): with --only, the fast drain reads commits and reconciles labels only for its target PR; the full pass keeps doing every PR.
